basis.judged: lane-A builder's rubric; opinion, labelled; lane J and the owner are the independent judges
basis.measured: raster of the shipped geometry at 40/70/160 px

benchmarks.lesson: restraint and one ink carry premium; the emblem is simple enough to stamp
benchmarks.structure: serif or slab capitals, generous tracking, small pictorial emblem (animal, landscape), one dark ink on natural ground, descriptor line with a founding date or place

benchmarks.lesson: type alone can be premium if the imagery is excellent
benchmarks.structure: lower-case geometric sans wordmark, no or abstract mark, photography does the emotional work, lots of white space

benchmarks.lesson: the illustration must have a simplified small-size cut or it fails as an icon
benchmarks.structure: monogram or initial with fine botanical line art, serif + italic pairing, hairline rules, muted sage/blush palette

benchmarks.lesson: the icon must read at 40 px; the grid of listing photos is the real brand
benchmarks.structure: square icon that is a simple initial or object on a flat colour; banners built from product photography; consistent thumbnail styling matters far more than the logo for clicks

benchmarks.lesson: a fruit mark drifts into 'jam brand' unless tied to the craft
benchmarks.structure: fruit illustration, rounded serif, warm reds

coherence: One B, one strand, one sprig across icon, emblem and motif.
laura_fit: Cream/sage/rose sits naturally with a warm, natural-light portrait and cream crochet; the mark is calm enough to sit beside a face.
ownable: A serif B alone is common; the B held in a yarn loop with a leaf pair, and the figure-of-eight emblem, make it Brambleloop's. Risk: monogram + botanical is a popular Etsy aesthetic, so execution quality matters.
owner_taste: Rebuilt directly from the owner's concept.
premium: High-contrast serif monogram, spaced capitals, hairline descriptor and a restrained sage/cream/rose palette: the structure of heritage and stationery houses, executed without clip-art.
story: Bramble (leaf, blossom, berry) + loop (yarn) + B, literally the name.

laura_fit: Neutral; cool charcoal fights a warm portrait slightly.
ownable: Two interlocked ovals are the universal 'hyperlink' / chain icon; the crochet meaning needs explaining -- the opposite of the owner's brief to stop looking like a software project.
premium: Clean and modern, but reads as a tech brand more than a pattern house.

coherence: Berry, drupelet motif and rounded serif agree.
ownable: A berry of bobble stitches with a looped stem is clever up close, but at 40 px it reads as a generic raspberry/grape icon.
owner_taste: Shares the palette mood and the bramble, not the monogram.
premium: Charming and warm; closer to a jam label than a design house.

coherence: Stitch grid unifies icon and motif.
laura_fit: Strong colour blocks compete with a portrait in a banner.
ownable: A B worked in V stitches is specific to the craft and unusual.
owner_taste: Different mood (indigo/saffron, modern) from the owner's concept.
premium: Graphic and confident; risks reading as a knitting app or pixel art.
story: Crochet and B; no bramble, no loop.

rubric_criteria.coherence: Do icon, emblem, wordmark, palette and motif read as one system?
rubric_criteria.laura_fit: Does it complement a warm, photographic Laura portrait rather than compete?
rubric_criteria.ownable: Could only Brambleloop own it? Is it free of generic yarn-ball / hook / flower / chain-icon readings?
rubric_criteria.owner_taste: Alignment with the owner's 2026-10-06 concept images (strong signal, not an automatic win).
rubric_criteria.premium: Would it sit beside a premium design-house or heritage-mill identity without looking template-made?
rubric_criteria.story: Does the mark tell the name (bramble + loop) and crochet without words?
